s365_phase1_projection.note: S365 Phase 1 correctly identifies the three most impactful infrastructure gaps but underestimates what post_change_qc.js can consolidate and misses the DL-021 governance guard rule (trivially cheap, closes a documented coverage gap). quick_wins.name: Fix generate_registry.js Section Mapping
quick_wins.description: The generate_registry.js script reads from build_master_registry.js CSV output but produces MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md with broken section labels (I/P/T/U instead of A-E). The root cause is an incomplete QID regex in extractQID() that fails to match Pack E and Pack C/D QID formats, coupled with a stale Domain field value in the CSV. Fix: (1) update the QID regex patterns in extractQID(); (2) ensure the Domain field maps correctly through the CSV → Markdown pipeline; (3) re-run npm run build-registry chain.
eliminates_manual_steps: Manual QID → Section cross-referencing when consuming registry
Distrust of registry output leading to raw-file grep workarounds
RULE 3 exception manual appends to MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md
quick_wins.implementation_notes: Fix extractQID() regex in generate_registry.js to cover all five QID formats (P1-X-NNN, P1B-X-NNN, P1-XC-NNN, P1-XD-NNN, P1E-X-NNN, P1-E-RNN). Verify Domain field flows correctly from pack_reader.js → build_master_registry.js CSV → generate_registry.js. Test: run npm run build-registry, verify section column shows A-F only.

quick_wins.name: DL-021 Governance Guard Rule (Rule 10)
quick_wins.description: Add a new BLOCK rule to governance-guard.js that prevents certification of items with structurally absent distractor ExplanationWrong fields. Currently: Rule 6 covers empty non-CC EW slots (DL-026) but absent fields (DL-021) pass through unchecked. 95 Certified Pack E Section C items have absent distractor EW fields — this rule would block any future certification that introduces the same gap. The detection logic already exists in findDL026Violations() — extend it to flag !(ewKey in obj) as a separate violation class.
eliminates_manual_steps: Manual DL-021 pre-certification scans that must be run separately
Post-certification discovery of absent distractor fields (expensive remediation)
Agent judgment about whether DL-021 is present (guard catches it mechanically)
quick_wins.implementation_notes: Extend findDL026Violations() or add findDL021Violations() to governance-guard.js. The check: for each non-CC letter, if !(ewKey in obj) → flag DL-021. Wire into tool.execute.before hook alongside existing Rule 6. Add 3 test cases to test_governance_guard.js (absent-field blocked, present-field passes, empty-string passes per Rule 6). ~30 lines of new code, ~20 lines of tests.

quick_wins.name: scan_dl031.js — Difficulty Inflation Detector
quick_wins.description: A regex-based scanner that identifies definition-match items with inflated difficulty labels (DL-031). Three-filter pipeline: (1) CognitiveLevel gate — only items with Remember/Understand AND DifficultyScore >= 3; (2) Definition-stem pattern gate — regex for 'Which of the following', 'refers to', 'is defined as', 'represents the'; (3) Stem-to-correct-choice lexical overlap — word-level Jaccard similarity > 50%. Output: scored candidate list sorted by confidence, with high-confidence matches auto-downgradable and borderline cases routed to verification queue.
eliminates_manual_steps: Manual cross-referencing of 1,154 DifficultyScore=3 items against CognitiveLevel fields
Per-item stem-vs-answer comparison for ~500 definition-match candidates
Manual Difficulty/DifficultyScore field replacement for confirmed matches
quick_wins.implementation_notes: Use pack_reader.js Function constructor for CC-position-aware extraction. Implement tri-filter pipeline: Filter 1 (field check), Filter 2 (regex patterns on Stem), Filter 3 (word-level Jaccard between Stem and correct Choice text, stop words removed). Output JSON: { qid, confidence, pattern_matches, suggest_downgrade }. Bulk-apply script for high-confidence matches (extractDL031CandidatesScanOnly mode default — no auto-apply without explicit flag). See S367 §1.1 and §3 for detailed methodology.

quick_wins.name: Registry Auto-Regeneration Hook
quick_wins.description: Add a post-write trigger to governance-guard.js that detects pack file modifications and appends a session-idle reminder to regenerate the registry. Does NOT auto-run the regeneration (that would require spawning a child process from the plugin, which is architecturally fragile). Instead, at session idle, if pack files were modified and the registry was not regenerated, the guard emits a Rule 10-level warning listing the exact command to run. This closes the staleness gap without introducing unsafe automatic writes.
eliminates_manual_steps: Remembering to regenerate registry after pack file changes
Manual timestamp checks to determine registry staleness
Out-of-sync registry causing agent confusion about certified/non-certified counts
quick_wins.implementation_notes: In governance-guard.js tool.execute.before: track whether any pack source file was written to (pack_*_corrected.js). In session.idle: if pack files touched AND registry timestamp is older than pack modification timestamps, emit a WARN-level message: 'Registry may be stale. Run: npm run build-registry'. No auto-regeneration (avoids process-spawn complexity and unintended side effects). ~20 lines of code.

medium_effort.name: pre_delivery_safety_check.js — Automated Delivery Pool Verification
medium_effort.description: A single-command script that automates the 7-step pre-delivery safety check currently performed manually per the pre-delivery-safety-check skill (155 lines of agent instructions). The script: (1) verifies question_state filter exists in app.js; (2) counts Certified items across all packs via Function constructor parse; (3) cross-references known-defective QID lists (DL-012 clones, DL-008 history, DL-034 missing fields); (4) verifies section coverage A-F; (5) spot-checks 5 random Certified items for structural integrity; (6) produces a structured JSON verdict. Run via: node scripts/pre_delivery_safety_check.js.
eliminates_manual_steps: Manual grep for question_state filter in app.js
Manual Certified count gathering across 5 packs
Manual cross-reference against DL-012 clone QID lists
Manual section coverage computation
Manual 5-item spot-check with per-field verification
Manual stop-condition adjudication
Manual verdict formatting
medium_effort.implementation_notes: Use pack_reader.js Function constructor for question_state extraction. Hardcode known-defective QID lists from DEFECT_LIBRARY.md (DL-012 clones, DL-008 re-contamination history, DL-034 missing-field items). Spot-check: verify CorrectChoice present, ExplanationWrong[CC] empty (Rule 2), ExplanationCorrect > 50 chars, 3 non-CC EW slots non-empty (Rule 6). Output JSON: { timestamp, certified_count, section_coverage: {A:N, B:N, ...}, known_defect_cross_reference: {...}, spot_checks: [...], stop_conditions: [...], verdict: 'SAFE'|'BLOCKED' }. See S365 §9 and pre-delivery-safety-check.md for requirements.

medium_effort.name: post_change_qc.js — Automated Post-Change QC Pipeline
medium_effort.description: A single-command script that executes all post-change quality-control steps currently performed manually (10 steps, ~15 minutes each). The script: (1) runs test_governance_guard.js — captures pass/fail count; (2) runs npm run validate — captures error/warning counts; (3) verifies QID counts unchanged via Function constructor parse on modified packs; (4) recaptures SHA-256 hashes for all 13 runtime-critical files; (5) diffs new hashes against stored baselines in CURRENT_BASELINES.md — flags drift; (6) re-scans modified packs for DL-008/DL-026/DL-037 using existing Function constructor scanners; (7) auto-updates CURRENT_BASELINES.md if hashes changed and --update-baselines flag set; (8) generates REVISION_HISTORY.md template entry with QID list and pass/fail counts; (9) outputs structured JSON QC report. This is the single highest-ROI automation investment per S367.
eliminates_manual_steps: Manual governance guard test invocation (51 tests)
Manual validator suite invocation with error/warning counting
Manual QID count verification via Select-String
Manual Get-FileHash for each modified pack file
Manual hash diff against CURRENT_BASELINES.md §5
Manual DL-008/DL-026/DL-037 re-scans
Manual CURRENT_BASELINES.md table row updates
Manual REVISION_HISTORY.md entry authoring
medium_effort.implementation_notes: Chain existing tools: child_process.execSync for governance guard tests + validator suite. Use pack_reader.js for QID counts. Use crypto.createHash('sha256') for hash capture (avoids PowerShell dependency). Parse CURRENT_BASELINES.md §1 table for stored hashes (read, regex-extract rows, diff). For DL-008/026/037 scans: require() scan_dl008_fn.js and scan_s710r_dl026.js logic inline, or execSync them. CURRENT_BASELINES.md update: read file, regex-replace matching table rows with new hashes, write back (safer than rebuild_baselines regex hacks because it operates on structured table format). REVISION_HISTORY.md template: generate markdown skeleton with before/after counts, QID list, scan results — agent fills in narrative and appends. ~300 lines of code. See S367 §1.5 for detailed friction-point analysis.

medium_effort.name: rebuild_baselines.js — Full Regeneration from Source
medium_effort.description: Replace the current rebuild_baselines_s*.js regex-replace hacks with a single regenerator that reads CURRENT_BASELINES.md, re-hashes all 13+ runtime-critical files from source, and rewrites the §1 table with current values. Unlike the current session-specific scripts (rebuild_baselines_s916.js, rebuild_baselines_s923.js, etc.) that regex-replace specific table rows, this script fully parses the markdown, recomputes all hashes, and writes a complete replacement. Also updates §2 (Certified Pool counts) by reading question_state from pack files via Function constructor.
eliminates_manual_steps: Manual Get-FileHash per modified file
Manual CURRENT_BASELINES.md §1 table editing
Manual Certified pool count extraction
Ad-hoc rebuild_baselines_sNNN.js script creation per session
medium_effort.implementation_notes: Key design: parse CURRENT_BASELINES.md into sections (read full file, split on '## N. ' headers). For §1: extract file paths from table rows, recompute SHA-256 via crypto.createHash('sha256'), write updated rows. For §2: use pack_reader.js Function constructor to count question_state: 'Certified' per pack, write updated counts. Preserve §3-6 and append a regeneration log entry at §6. Avoid the regex-replace anti-pattern entirely — work with parsed table structures. Consolidate all rebuild_baselines_s*.js into backups/ and archive them. ~150 lines of code.

high_effort.name: CI/CD Pipeline — GitHub Actions on Push
high_effort.description: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that runs automatically on push: (1) npm run validate (validator suite); (2) node scripts/test_governance_guard.js (governance guard 51 tests); (3) node scripts/pre_delivery_safety_check.js (delivery pool integrity); (4) node scripts/rebuild_baselines.js --check-only (hash drift detection, no write). Any failure blocks the PR merge. This moves from 0/10 CI/CD to a baseline automated gate. Requires: .github/workflows/ci.yml file, npm scripts organization, and reconciling the repo's private/non-GitHub status (the repo may not be hosted on GitHub — the CI concept applies to any Git forge).
eliminates_manual_steps: Manual 'did I break anything?' checks before considering a session complete
Late discovery of regressions introduced days earlier
Manual cross-session drift reconciliation (G1-G5 runbook)
T0/Tmid/Tend checkpoint sequence being fully manual (AGENTS.md §13.1)
high_effort.implementation_notes: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml: on push to any branch, checkout, setup Node.js, npm ci (if package-lock.json exists), run validate → test_governance_guard → pre_delivery_safety_check → rebuild_baselines --check-only. For repos not hosted on GitHub: the workflow file doubles as documentation of the canonical CI sequence; alternative runners (GitLab CI, local git hooks) can replicate. Add npm scripts: 'npm run ci' wraps all four checks. This is infrastructure, not content — zero CAQS verification required.

high_effort.name: clone_replacement_scaffolder.js — Metadata Scaffolding for New Items
high_effort.description: A script that pre-populates all 12+ structural metadata fields for cloned/archived item replacement slots. Manual Section/Part/Domain field population
Manual ItemType/ItemStyle assignment per QID convention
Manual VerifiedChecks boilerplate population

Manual replacement_lineage_tracker entry

high_effort.name: Script Hygiene Catalog & Archive Pass
high_effort.description: Taxonomize all 224 top-level scripts in scripts/ and archive confirmed one-offs, delete abandoned prototypes, and create a structured index. The current 53.1% uncategorized rate (119 scripts) means nearly half the scripts/ directory is opaque to any new agent or contributor. The SESSION950 index catalogs 22 uncertain scripts as a start; ~97 remain unexamined. This is a one-time investment with permanent benefits: every future session spends less time figuring out which script to run.
eliminates_manual_steps: Agent confusion about which scanner to invoke for a given defect type
Time lost opening and reading abandoned one-off scripts
Risk of invoking a DL-029-vulnerable forward-scan script (check_ew.js, session86_*.js)
Uncertainty about whether a script is production-grade or session-specific
high_effort.implementation_notes: Three-pass approach: Pass 1 (quick skim — classify by filename pattern: sNNN_* = session-specific, scan_* = defect scanner, build_* = generator, test_* = test, _* = abandoned). Pass 2 (deep read — open each uncertain script, read first 20 lines, classify by function). Pass 3 (archive — move confirmed one-offs to scripts/archive/, add .archive suffix to abandoned prototypes, update SESSION950 index with full taxonomy). Flag any script using forward-scan regex (DL-029 risk) — these must never be invoked for production decisions. Create scripts/README.md with structured taxonomy. ~8 hours because each of 67 uncertain scripts requires 30-60 sec of reading + classification + decision.

verdict.rationale: All Phase 1 components are additive — new scripts and one guard rule extension. No existing infrastructure needs to be redesigned. The pack_reader.js engine provides reliable Function constructor parsing for all new scripts. The governance guard plugin architecture supports additional rules without refactoring. The only architectural concern is the CI/CD component (Phase 2) which requires the repo to be hosted on a Git forge with CI runner support — but the Phase 1 55-target package does not depend on CI/CD.
verdict.biggest_risk: The rebuild_baselines.js regenerator must correctly parse CURRENT_BASELINES.md's §1 table structure. The table format has been stable across 40+ manual updates, but edge cases (multiple provenance entries per cell, TBD placeholder values) need handling. Fallback: if table parsing proves fragile, the regenerator can use the simpler approach of reading file paths from a hardcoded manifest and writing a complete new §1 section — this eliminates the parsing ambiguity entirely.
verdict.next_session: S370-A — Implement the first 2-3 QUICK WINS: Fix generate_registry.js + DL-021 governance guard Rule 10 + scan_dl031.js. These three changes take ~3 hours total, add +3 to automation score (48→51), and establish the pattern for the remaining Phase 1 components.
